Location and internet features are off by default. Without them, CamperLog works completely offline.
Location (optional): only when you tap “Use current location”, CamperLog reads your position once and saves it with the stop. Never in the background, never sent anywhere.

Weather & map (optional): CamperLog has the internet permission but only uses it when you turn this on. Getting the weather sends the stop’s coordinates, rounded to about 1 km, to Open-Meteo. The map loads the area you are looking at from OpenStreetMap. Both services see your IP address.

Notifications (optional): off by default. Turning them on asks for the notification permission and runs a daily background check for due maintenance and your backup reminder, entirely on your device. For that check the app also holds two permissions granted at installation without a prompt: starting again after a restart and briefly keeping the device awake; they are only used while notifications are on. Nothing is ever sent anywhere.
No account, no ads, no analytics. Nothing else ever leaves your device.

Google plans to require every Android app — including ones installed outside the Play Store, like this one — to come from a verified developer identity, starting in 2026. Without that verification, devices will refuse to install apps at all.

This would hit F-Droid especially hard: an independent, sideloadable app store like F-Droid may no longer be able to exist in its current form, and continued maintenance of CamperLog outside Google's control could become impossible.

The "Keep Android Open" campaign is fighting these plans.
